name: Illustrative AI governance starter
note: Synthetic sandbox only. These examples are not company policy or legal advice. Revise the rubric and prompts with Ralph and Jeremy before any operational use.

dimensions.label: Data confidentiality and privacy
dimensions.guidance: Consider the sensitivity of the inputs and outputs, not just the name of the tool. Personal, confidential, privileged, or proprietary data increases exposure. Do not infer a data classification or permission that the request does not state.
anchors: Entirely public or synthetic material, with no personal or confidential information.
Routine internal non-sensitive information, with expressly stated appropriate handling.
Personal or confidential information with stated appropriate handling and safeguards.
Sensitive personal or privileged information, or confidential data with explicitly inadequate handling.

dimensions.label: Security, vendor exposure, and data handling
dimensions.guidance: Consider access restrictions, external sharing, retention, vendor training, and the stated tool approval. Unknown vendor terms must stay unknown; do not look up or assume real vendor practices.
anchors: Public or synthetic data in an isolated read-only workflow, with explicit access, sharing, and retention boundaries.
Named restricted users and stated suitable vendor handling, with no material integration privileges.
External processing or integrations with stated controls but meaningful residual exposure.
Explicitly unapproved sensitive-data processing, unrestricted sensitive access, or inadequate deletion or sharing controls.

dimensions.label: Autonomy and human oversight
dimensions.guidance: Distinguish drafting and recommendations from actual decisions or actions. Consider the human approval point and the ability to stop or reverse actions.
anchors: Read-only synthesis or a synthetic demonstration; a human checks the result before any use.
Low-impact drafting with mandatory human review and no authority to act.
Bounded low-impact actions with monitoring, reversibility, and explicit limits.
Consequential decisions or actions, especially without prior human approval.

dimensions.label: Impact on people, operations, and safety
dimensions.guidance: Assess who could be affected by an error. Employment, legal obligations, physical safety, or material financial commitments require special care. Cite only this sample rubric, not invented laws.
anchors: No operational consequence beyond exploration of public or synthetic information.
Reversible internal productivity use with limited consequences for errors.
Customer-facing or operational use with meaningful but bounded consequences.
Employment, rights, legal obligations, physical safety, or material financial consequences.

dimensions.label: Output reliability and intended audience
dimensions.guidance: Consider how errors will be detected and whether outputs are internal, external, factual, or consequential. Human review must be described, not assumed.
anchors: Human-checked summaries grounded in public or synthetic source material, without consequential reliance.
Human-checked internal drafts with source checking and a clear owner.
External or operational outputs with review and validation but meaningful residual error risk.
Unverified outputs used for consequential decisions, represented as authoritative, or acted on without validation.

dimensions.label: Intellectual property and permitted use
dimensions.guidance: Check whether input use and the intended use of outputs are expressly permitted. Publicly available is not the same as freely licensed. Do not assume copyright status or contractual terms.
anchors: Synthetic, owned, or expressly permitted inputs and outputs used within those permissions.
Expressly licensed third-party material used within stated license limits, with required attribution.
Commercial or external reuse with stated permissions but material residual licensing or ownership questions.
Explicitly unauthorized input use or output reuse outside stated permissions.

blocking_rules.label: Sensitive data sent to an explicitly unsuitable vendor
blocking_rules.rule: Applies when confidential, personal, privileged, or proprietary non-public data will be sent to a tool explicitly stated to be unapproved for that data, or used for vendor training without permission. Public-only or synthetic-only data does not trigger this rule. For sensitive data with unknown approval or training terms, return unknown. This is an illustrative sandbox restriction.

blocking_rules.label: Consequential action without prior human approval
blocking_rules.rule: Applies when AI will directly make or execute consequential decisions about employment, customer rights, legal obligations, physical safety, or material financial commitments without prior human approval. Human-reviewed drafts and recommendations do not trigger this rule. When autonomy or approval is unspecified, return unknown. This is an illustrative sandbox restriction.
